A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BayesVLM work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original zero-shot classification, calibration, active-learning, runtime, and approximation-quality results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional proxy-data and hyperparameter-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions use independent last-layer Laplace approximations, KFAC/GGN covariance estimation, ProbCosine, probit predictions, and the same Bayesian active-learning updates. v4 expands the mathematical formulation and computational explanation without establishing a new operational component or changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 adds CC12M as a proxy source for estimating CLIP's Hessian, alongside LAION-400M (Section 4.3, Table 3). CC12M previously appeared as PCME++ checkpoint provenance, rather than this BayesVLM evaluation scenario. The downstream classification and active-learning datasets and tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain vanilla CLIP/SigLIP, temperature scaling, Farina et al.'s TTA, PCME++ and ProLIP mean predictions, and the same active-learning acquisition comparisons. The new CC12M comparison varies BayesVLM's Hessian data source rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: New sensitivity protocols sweep pseudo-counts {1,3,5,7,9} and batch sizes {2048,8192,32768} using 1–5 batches. v4 Appendix F.8 reports a default pseudo-count of 4, whereas v3 Figure 8 identifies 10 for CLIP-Base. v4 retains that old caption, leaving the exact applied setting inconsistent. Existing metrics and fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands robustness testing: a controlled CC12M-versus-LAION Hessian comparison, pseudo-count sensitivity across four classification benchmarks, and negative-sample/batch-size sensitivity for both modalities. These extend beyond v3's validation-set tuning curve and sample-count analysis. The earlier corruption example, approximation-quality check, and k-NN ablation are retained.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports means and standard deviations over five trials for the new negative-sample analysis (Appendix F.9, Figures 5 and 15). Existing test-set standard errors, paired t-tests at p=0.05, and the ten-subset Hessian analysis remain. This does not establish increased repetitions of the earlier experiments.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial proxy-data and sensitivity results and revises BayesVLM entries in Table 1 and the CLIP-Large/SigLIP appendix tables. For example, CLIP-Base Food-101 ECE changes from 1.91 to 1.69, while SigLIP UCF101 ECE changes from 7.87 to 9.60. These are revised reported values, not established same-setting gains, given the hyperparameter ambiguity. PCME++, ProLIP, runtime, and active-learning results are retained.

T1.justification: v3 begins its posterior derivation by assuming independent projections. v4 adds a coupled, non-i.i.d. loss/GGN derivation and explicitly formulates modality-conditional likelihoods in Appendices C.1 and C.2.1. Appendix C.2.2 also adds efficient Hessian algebra and substantially revises the marginal-likelihood expression. This is a substantial formal expansion of the retained method.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about training-free uncertainty estimation, ProbCosine, and active learning remain. v4's introduction and conclusion additionally emphasize robustness, including use with proprietary pretraining data. The claim to a first Bayesian VLM formulation was already present in v3.

C2.justification: v4 explains why conditioning on jointly trained MAP estimates can retain cross-modal information despite factorization, and adds a warning about relying only on expected cosine similarity under corruption. Its limitations discussion softens the original-training-data requirement and emphasizes proxy-data robustness; v3 already evaluated a SigLIP proxy but warned about Hessian degeneration.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix C.2.2 supplies explicit Hessian contractions and matrix dimensions explaining how to avoid materializing a roughly 32k-by-32k loss Hessian; v3 only mentions rearranging terms. The expanded reproducibility statement mainly organizes existing information. The code-access address, hardware, checkpoints, and fine-tuning recipe were already disclosed in v3.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ju et al. and Lafon et al. on VLM uncertainty, plus references supporting NLPD, non-i.i.d. inference, and GGN computation. Much of the earlier related-work discussion moves into Appendix B.1. The fundamental positioning as training-free, post-hoc Bayesian uncertainty estimation remains.

P1.justification: v4 broadly rewrites the introduction, contribution narrative, likelihood/Hessian explanation, and several active-learning and experimental paragraphs. It condenses the main related-work section while moving detailed discussion into Appendix B.1, reorganizes the derivations, and expands the brief reproducibility note into a structured statement.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document template, title/header treatment, typography, and display placement. It adds the proxy-data table, repeated as Table 13, the pseudo-count table, and negative-sample plots with a repeated main-text panel. The earlier FLOPs table and corruption figure move to Appendix F, and Figure 8 is redrawn with different axes and curves. Most existing scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the central approximation more transparent and adds controlled proxy-data and sensitivity checks that strengthen empirical support for practical use. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix F.8's default pseudo-count of 4 conflicts with Figure 8's retained caption, and UCF101 ECE is 3.57 in Table 1 but 3.77 in Tables 3 and 13. The additions improve assessability, but leave important settings and robustness claims incompletely reconciled.
